evals.name: pulls-page-logic
evals.prompt: The PR list page in client/src/app/repos/[repoId]/pulls/page.tsx does a bunch of filtering, searching, sorting and counting inline. Clean it up so the logic lives where it should in this codebase.
evals.expected_output: Pure filter/sort/count helpers in pulls/helpers.ts with a helpers.test.ts, OPEN_STATUSES moved to pulls/constants.ts, page.tsx only composes; no utils/ folder, no pseudo-hooks, no unrelated edits.
expectations: Filtering, search and sorting logic moves out of page.tsx into pure function(s) in the route's pulls/helpers.ts
The open / needs-review counting moves out of page.tsx into a pure helper
OPEN_STATUSES (the open-status set) moves from page.tsx into pulls/constants.ts
A unit test for the new helpers is proposed (e.g. pulls/helpers.test.ts)
No utils/ folder or catch-all utils/common module is created
New functions that call no React hooks are not named use* and do not import React
Source-code changes stay within the pulls route (page, helpers, constants, their test); no unrelated source file is refactored

Behaviour is preserved: header counts use the unfiltered list, sorting does not mutate the query data, and filter/search/sort semantics (status 'all', title-or-number match, newest by default, missing dates as 0) are unchanged
Stale file:line citations to the pulls page in client/specs/pages.md and e2e/specs/flows.md are corrected in place in the same change and match the edited files; INSIGHTS.md is not edited by hand
The proposed diffs apply to the current files, the proposed helpers.test.ts passes, and the result typechecks (verify on a scratch copy)

evals.name: dedupe-format-and-colors
evals.prompt: formatWhen is copy-pasted in ReviewRunAccordion and in diff-viewer's CommentCard, and there are two severity colour maps (FindingCard's constants and the FindingsSection inside RunTraceDrawer) that don't even agree with each other. Fix the duplication.
evals.expected_output: One formatter in src/lib/<purpose>.ts imported by both; one severity colour map owned by a shared module, typed by the Severity union; the --sugg vs --accent conflict surfaced for the user to decide; no utils/ or export * barrels.
expectations: The formatWhen replacement lives in one shared module outside src/app (src/lib/<purpose>.ts or similar), named for its purpose, not utils.ts
Both ReviewRunAccordion.tsx and diff-viewer/CommentCard.tsx import the shared formatter and their local copies are removed
No new severity colour map is created: FindingCard and FindingsSection both reuse the design system's existing SEV from @devdigest/ui
The --accent -> --sugg token change appears in the proposal's questions for the user (not only in the rationale), with a note on whether it is visible
The defensive fallback for unknown severity values in FindingsSection is preserved, so behaviour for bad stored data is unchanged
No new utils/ folder and no new `export *` barrel is introduced
The shared formatter keeps formatWhen's exact behaviour (same body/output, including returning the input for an invalid date)
Contract docs citing moved ReviewRunAccordion/CommentCard lines (client/specs/pages.md, e2e/specs/flows.md) are corrected in place, or the proposal shows that no cited line moves

evals.name: run-filters-component
evals.prompt: On the PR page's Review runs tab I want a filter bar above the runs: chips to filter by agent and by verdict (approve / request changes / comment). Plan where every piece goes and write the code for it.
evals.expected_output: Route-local _components/RunFilters/ with RunFilters.tsx + index.ts + constants.ts + helpers.ts (+ tests) + styles.ts; labels in messages/en/prReview.json; style={s.x}; pure filter helper; no new fetch; selection owned by the parent (or URL).
expectations: The filter bar is a route-local component under pulls/[number]/_components/<Name>/ with <Name>.tsx and index.ts
Styling uses a colocated styles.ts consumed as style={s.x}; no Tailwind utility classNames
New UI copy (group labels, empty state) is added as keys in messages/en/prReview.json, and the existing verdict label keys are reused rather than duplicated
Run-filtering logic is a pure helper (helpers.ts), not inline in JSX, and a unit test for it is proposed
No new network call: no fetch/api usage and no new query hook; it reuses already-loaded review data
Filter options / verdict keys are module-level constants (constants.ts), typed via as const or the Verdict union
Selection state has a single owner (the parent rendering the runs, or the URL) and is passed to the bar via props
Chips use @devdigest/ui primitives (e.g. Chip) rather than new hand-built buttons

A constant map needed by a second component (e.g. VerdictBanner's VERDICT_META) is moved to the nearest common level (route-level constants) instead of being imported from a sibling component's folder
Integration with existing behaviour is handled: a Timeline jump to a filtered-out run still works, and changing a filter does not re-scroll to a stale Timeline target
After a filter change at most one run accordion is open, or the proposal otherwise prevents two FindingsPanels from handling j/k/a/d at once
The stale-Timeline-target case (a filter change must not re-scroll to an old jump target) is covered by a proposed test
Contract docs citing shifted FindingsTab/ReviewRunAccordion lines (client/specs/pages.md, e2e/specs/flows.md) are corrected in place, not left stale or only annotated

evals.name: hook-vs-helper-promotion
evals.prompt: The findings list inside the run trace drawer (FindingsSection) should get the same 'Hide low confidence' toggle that FindingsPanel has on the Review runs tab. Add a useVisibleFindings(findings, hideLow) hook so both components share the filtering.
evals.expected_output: Explains that useVisibleFindings(findings, hideLow) calls no hooks, so it should be the existing pure visibleFindings helper promoted with its constants to the pulls/[number] route rung; FindingsPanel re-imports from there; toggle state stays local in FindingsSection; existing hideLowConfidence copy reused; helper test.
expectations: The shared filtering is a plain non-use* pure function; the proposal explains that useVisibleFindings(findings, hideLow) would call no hooks, or makes the hook genuinely stateful and says why
The existing visibleFindings logic from FindingsPanel/helpers.ts is reused instead of rewriting the filter

The shared helper and the constants it needs (LOW_CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD, severity order) move to the route rung (pulls/[number]/helpers.ts / constants.ts) or reuse shared equivalents, and are never imported from FindingsPanel's folder
FindingsPanel imports from the new location and no copy of the helper or its constants remains in its folder
The hide-low toggle state stays local to FindingsSection (not lifted into context or a global store)
A unit test for the promoted helper is proposed
The toggle label reuses the existing prReview hideLowConfidence message (or another messages/en key), not hardcoded English

evals.name: server-fetch-decision
evals.prompt: Make the /agents page load the agent list on the server so it renders without the loading skeleton.
evals.expected_output: Flags that nothing fetches on the server today and this adds a second data path, asks before applying; if proposing, prefetches ['agents'] into a per-request QueryClient via the existing api client and hydrates with HydrationBoundary, keeping page.tsx a thin server component and 'use client' on AgentsListView, with client invalidation intact.
expectations: The proposal identifies that nothing in client/ fetches on the server today and that this adds a second data path, and asks the user to confirm before applying

TanStack Query stays the owner of the agent list: the server only prefetches into a per-request QueryClient under the same ['agents'] key and hydrates it (HydrationBoundary/dehydrate), instead of passing raw agents as props
The server-side request goes through the existing api client (src/lib/api.ts) or a server-only module, not an ad-hoc fetch() in page.tsx
page.tsx stays a thin Server Component and "use client" stays on AgentsListView (not added to page.tsx)
Existing client behaviour still works: create/delete invalidation and refetch through useAgents, and loading/error handling on client-side navigation
